- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–8% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum (last 5 prices rising) and forecast continues rising, check for lag — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 periods.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6) and forecast is erratic, smooth out extremes by averaging with prior 3-day moving average.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by >2% over 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward correction for next 5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a spike, reduce forecast peak by 10–15% and shift mean to earlier period.
